nodes.summary: For a natural number $k \ge 2$ and a natural number $n$, the base-$k$ expansion of $n$ is the word $d_1 d_2 \cdots d_m$ of base-$k$ digits, most significant digit first, with $n = \sum_{i=1}^{m} d_i k^{m-i}$ and $d_1 \neq 0$; for $n = 0$ it is the empty word.
nodes.title: Base-k expansion

nodes.summary: The value of a word $w = d_1 d_2 \cdots d_m$ of base-$k$ digits $d_i \in \{0, \dots, k - 1\}$, read with the most significant digit first, is $\sum_{i=1}^{m} d_i k^{m-i}$. The empty word has value $0$.
nodes.title: Value of a base-k digit word

nodes.summary: Two natural numbers $k$ and $l$ are multiplicatively independent when $k^m \ne l^n$ for all positive natural numbers $m$ and $n$.
nodes.title: Multiplicatively independent bases

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be multiplicatively independent natural numbers with $l \ge 2$, and let $S$ be a set of natural numbers that is recognizable in base $k$ and whose characteristic sequence $n \mapsto (n \in S)$, a sequence of truth values, is not ultimately periodic. Then $S$ is not recognizable in base $l$.
nodes.title: Cobham's theorem for characteristic sequences

nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $l$ be multiplicatively independent natural numbers with $l \ge 2$, and let $S$ be a set of natural numbers that is recognizable in base $k$ and is not ultimately periodic. Then $S$ is not recognizable in base $l$.
nodes.title: Cobham's theorem

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number and let $x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers whose set of values is recognizable in base $k$. Then either the limit superior, as $i \to \infty$, of the ratios $x_{i+1} / x_i$ computed in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ (where a ratio with denominator $0$ is $\infty$) is greater than $1$, or there is a natural number $C$ with…
nodes.title: Cobham's gap theorem without a separate base hypothesis

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 2$ be a natural number and let $x_0 < x_1 < x_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of natural numbers whose set of values is recognizable in base $k$. Then either the limit superior, as $i \to \infty$, of the ratios $x_{i+1} / x_i$ computed in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$ (so an unbounded limit superior is $\infty$, and a ratio with denominator $0$ is $\infty$) is greater than…
nodes.title: Cobham's gap theorem

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$, a set $S$ of natural numbers is recognizable in base $k$ when $k \ge 2$ and some deterministic finite automaton with a nonempty finite set of states, reading words of base-$k$ digits from the most significant digit, accepts a word $w = d_1 d_2 \cdots d_m$ exactly when $w$ is canonical (empty, or with $d_1 \neq 0$) and its value $\sum_{i=1}^{m} d_i k^{m-i}$ lies in $S$.
nodes.title: Sets recognizable in base k

nodes.summary: A word of base-$k$ digits is canonical when it is empty or its first (most significant) digit is nonzero.
nodes.title: Canonical base-k words

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of natural numbers is ultimately periodic if and only if its characteristic sequence $n \mapsto (n \in S)$, a sequence of truth values, is ultimately periodic.
nodes.title: Ultimately periodic sets and their characteristic sequences

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of natural numbers is ultimately periodic when there are natural numbers $N$ and $p > 0$ such that, for every $n \ge N$, $n \in S$ if and only if $n + p \in S$.
nodes.title: Ultimately periodic sets of natural numbers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
